name: New Orleans, LA
local_context: New Orleans (Orleans Parish) layers state tax credits from the Louisiana Housing Corporation with city gap funds, Finance New Orleans bonds and PILOTs, and HANO project-based vouchers. Location matters a lot here: historic, cultural and downtown districts unlock the state historic credit and the Restoration Tax Abatement, while inclusionary zoning applies only in certain sub-districts. City gap funding has been tight since 2025, and the inclusionary mandate is under review after a November 2025 study recommended ending it.

miz.label: Mandatory Inclusionary Zoning sub-district
miz.display: the {name} of the Mandatory Inclusionary Zoning overlay

about.title: Mandatory Inclusionary Zoning (MIZ)
about.text: A zoning overlay where new rental buildings with 10 or more units must include affordable units, kept affordable for 99 years at 60% of area median income: 10% of units in the Core sub-district (Central Business District and French Quarter) and 5% in the Strong sub-districts. Developers can pay a fee in lieu instead.
about.meaning: A market-rate project here needs to budget for affordable units or the fee. A fully affordable project already meets the requirement. A November 2025 city study recommended ending the mandate, so check whether it's still in force.

about.title: Local historic district
about.text: A city-designated historic district. Exterior changes, demolitions and new construction need approval from the Historic District Landmarks Commission, or the Vieux Carré Commission in the French Quarter.
about.meaning: Plan extra time for design review. Being in a historic district also counts toward the Restoration Tax Abatement.

Vieux Carré.title: Vieux Carré (French Quarter) historic district
Vieux Carré.text: The French Quarter's local historic district. The Vieux Carré Commission reviews exterior work, demolitions and new construction.
Vieux Carré.meaning: Expect detailed design review. The location counts toward the Restoration Tax Abatement.

about.title: National Register historic district
about.text: An area listed by the National Park Service as historically significant. Listing doesn't restrict what private owners do with their buildings.
about.meaning: Renovating a contributing building can qualify for the 20% federal and 25% Louisiana historic rehabilitation tax credits, which can be combined with LIHTC.

about.title: Louisiana Cultural District
about.text: A state-designated arts and culture district (created by Act 298 of 2007). The sales tax break on original art sold in these districts ended January 1, 2025.
about.meaning: Renovating a historic building (over 50 years old) here can qualify for the 25% Louisiana historic rehabilitation credit even if it isn't on the National Register.

about.title: Special taxing or improvement district
about.text: A district created under Louisiana law that usually adds a small tax or fee inside its boundary to pay for extra services, such as security, cleaning or economic development.
about.meaning: It can add to a building's annual operating costs. Some types also make a site eligible for incentives such as the Restoration Tax Abatement.

Downtown Development District.title: Downtown Development District (DDD)
Downtown Development District.text: Created by the Legislature in 1974 as the country's first assessment-based business improvement district. Downtown owners pay an extra property tax (13.73 mills in 2025) for enhanced cleaning, 24-hour security, homeless outreach and economic development.
Downtown Development District.meaning: Adds a modest amount to property taxes, but a downtown development district location qualifies for the 25% Louisiana historic credit and the Restoration Tax Abatement.

BioDistrict.title: BioDistrict New Orleans
BioDistrict.text: A state-created political subdivision (R.S. 33:9039.61) meant to grow the biosciences and medical economy around the downtown medical center. A 15-member board governs it, and it has taxing and bonding authority. A 2022 law (Act 354) took away its power to expropriate property and requires a PILOT agreement with the city before it buys property.
BioDistrict.meaning: It doesn't offer housing subsidies itself. Large projects may want to coordinate with the district's plans.

patterns.title: Economic development district
patterns.text: A Louisiana economic development district can levy up to 2% in extra sales or hotel taxes inside its boundary, often to repay financing for a specific development (R.S. 33:9038.39).
patterns.meaning: Customers of commercial space may pay a slightly higher sales tax. The location counts as an economic development district for the Restoration Tax Abatement.

patterns.title: Neighborhood improvement or security district
patterns.text: Property owners pay an annual parcel fee, set by voters for terms of up to five years (often $100 to $600 per parcel), for extra patrols or beautification.
patterns.meaning: Add the parcel fee to the operating budget.

patterns.title: Neighborhood security district
patterns.text: Property owners pay an annual parcel fee, set by voters for terms of up to five years, for extra patrols.
patterns.meaning: Add the parcel fee to the operating budget.

about.title: Tax increment financing (TIF) district
about.text: Growth in sales or property taxes inside the boundary is set aside to repay the costs of a specific development. New Orleans' TIF districts are mostly tied to individual projects.
about.meaning: A new project would need to negotiate with the district to share in any increment.

programs.name: Louisiana Housing Corporation: 9% and 4% LIHTC allocation
programs.summary: LHC allocates Louisiana's federal housing tax credits through its Qualified Allocation Plan. The 2025 QAP (amended January 13, 2026) covers a two-year ceiling, with an estimated $26 million added for 2026. Recent QAPs emphasize cost containment and housing for seniors, single-parent households and domestic violence survivors.
programs.amount: Credit amount set by eligible basis; 2026 statewide ceiling estimated at $26 million
programs.eligibility: Competitive (9%) or bond-financed (4%). Read the current QAP for set-asides, scoring and cost limits.
programs.deadline: Set by the QAP round; no 2026-specific round confirmed as of October 2026.

project_rules.fail: This program funds rental housing only.
LIHTC units must be restricted to 60% AMI or below (or average 60% under income averaging).

programs.name: LHC HOME and Housing Trust Fund gap financing for LIHTC projects
programs.summary: LHC has offered up to $2,000,000 per project in HOME and National Housing Trust Fund money to 4% and 9% LIHTC projects that are already awarded, still in predevelopment, and have a documented funding gap. Applications are first come, first served until funds run out, and a pre-submission meeting is required.
programs.eligibility: Only for projects with an existing LIHTC award. The program description found is undated, so confirm it is still open with LHC.

project_rules.fail: This program funds rental housing only.
This gap money is for LIHTC projects, which serve 60% AMI or below.

programs.name: Louisiana State Commercial Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit
programs.agency: Louisiana Division of Historic Preservation (Office of Cultural Development)
programs.summary: State income and franchise tax credit for rehabilitating historic income-producing buildings, including residential rentals. The credit is 25% of eligible rehabilitation costs (35% in rural areas, which excludes New Orleans). It stacks with the 20% federal historic credit and can be combined with LIHTC.
programs.amount: 25% of eligible rehabilitation costs incurred January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2028
programs.eligibility: The building must be individually listed on, or contributing to a district on, the National Register, or be in a Downtown Development District or a state cultural district. Only costs incurred before January 1, 2029 qualify (the program sunsets December 31, 2028).
programs.deadline: Rolling reservations through the Division of Historic Preservation, subject to the $85 million annual cap

area.outside_note: Site is not in a National Register district, cultural district or the Downtown Development District, and the building at this address isn't individually listed. It could still qualify if the building is eligible for listing.

project_rules.fail: Only for renovating an existing building.
The commercial historic credit covers income-producing buildings such as rentals.

references.title: Louisiana Department of Revenue: changes to the historic structures rehabilitation credit

programs.limits: Statewide reservations are capped at $85 million a year (Part 2 applications received on or after January 1, 2025), and no taxpayer, with affiliates, may claim more than $5 million a year for structures in any one downtown development or cultural district.

programs.name: Restoration Tax Abatement (RTA)
programs.agency: City of New Orleans Office of Economic Development, with Louisiana Economic Development
programs.summary: For renovating or expanding an existing building, the owner keeps paying property tax on the pre-project assessed value for five years after completion. The state adopted rule changes effective June 20, 2026, and the City's 2025 rules (R-25-274) apply to Advance Notifications filed on or after May 22, 2025.
programs.amount: Property tax frozen at pre-project value for 5 years
programs.eligibility: Existing structures only, in a downtown development, economic development or historic district, or an Opportunity Zone. The City's FAQ lists commercial projects and owner-occupied residences; multi-unit rentals are likely treated as commercial, so confirm with the Office of Economic Development. Short-term rentals are prohibited during the abatement. Advance Notification and Application must be filed in FastLane before construction starts.
programs.deadline: Before construction begins; the City's review committee meets periodically

project_rules.fail: Only for renovating an existing building.

programs.name: City of New Orleans housing gap financing (NOFAs)
programs.agency: City of New Orleans Office of Housing Policy and Community Development
programs.summary: The City periodically releases funding notices for affordable rental projects, using HUD funds (CDBG, HOME), bond proceeds and housing trust fund dollars. The most recent round found was a September 2025 CDBG Affordable Rental Rehabilitation NOFA ($5 million, rehab of existing rentals). In 2025 the office reported receiving only $24 million of a promised $32 million for previously awarded gap financing, so new money is limited.
programs.amount: Varies by NOFA; city subsidy historically covers about 10-15% of total development cost
programs.eligibility: Affordable rental units for income-qualified households; terms set by each NOFA.
programs.deadline: No 2026 new-construction round found as of October 2026; watch the City's funding page.

project_rules.fail: City affordable housing funds serve households at or below 80% AMI.

funding.note: No 2026 new-construction funding round found as of October 2026.

programs.name: Finance New Orleans: multifamily bonds, PILOTs and green loans
programs.agency: Finance New Orleans (Finance Authority of New Orleans)
programs.summary: A quasi-governmental lender whose board is appointed by the City Council. Under a 2020 agreement with the City and LHC, it can pair its multifamily revenue bonds with LHC's non-competitive 4% tax credits, and offer PILOTs and green infrastructure loans to developers.
programs.eligibility: Affordable or mixed-income multifamily projects; terms negotiated per deal.

project_rules.fail: This program funds rental housing only.
Finance New Orleans multifamily bonds are for multifamily projects (5+ units).

programs.name: Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) for affordable housing
programs.summary: A PILOT replaces full property taxes with a fixed, lower payment in exchange for affordable units. The City defines affordable housing as up to 60% of area median income and workforce housing as 61-120%. Recent examples include the Rivana apartments in the River District (Council review June 2026). The IDB's PILOT policies were approved March 12, 2025.
programs.eligibility: Case by case. In April 2026 the Council President asked the IDB to pause new PILOT approvals pending a citywide economic development plan, so check current status before counting on one.
programs.deadline: Rolling, subject to IDB and Council approval

project_rules.fail: This program funds rental housing only.
PILOTs are tied to affordable (60% AMI) or workforce (up to 120% AMI) units.

funding.note: In April 2026 the Council President asked the Industrial Development Board to pause new PILOT approvals.

programs.name: HANO Project-Based Vouchers
programs.summary: Long-term rental assistance attached to units, which supports debt sizing. HANO's most recent solicitation offered up to 300 general vouchers for family projects plus up to 500 exception vouchers for properties serving elderly, disabled, homeless or veteran households, or in census tracts with under 20% poverty.
programs.eligibility: New construction or substantial rehab with at least 10 PBV units. General vouchers are capped at 25% of units or 120 units, whichever is less.
programs.deadline: Check hano.org for the current solicitation; a 2026 date was not confirmed.

project_rules.fail: This program funds rental housing only.
HANO requires at least 10 project-based voucher units.

programs.name: NORA land and NOHIP construction financing
programs.agency: New Orleans Redevelopment Authority (NORA) and NORU
programs.summary: NORA sells city-held vacant lots, and its affiliate NORU provides construction loans and subsidy through the New Orleans Housing Investment Program (NOHIP). The 2026 NOHIP round, for single-family homes for households at or below 80% AMI, closed August 6, 2026. NORA also auctioned 140+ lots in September 2026 with minimum bids as low as $4,000.
programs.amount: Discounted lots; NORU construction financing and subsidy
programs.eligibility: Mostly homeownership. Builds must meet Energy Star, FORTIFIED and NORA resilience standards; auction buyers must finish within 18 months.
programs.deadline: 2026 NOHIP round closed; watch NORA for the next round and auctions

project_rules.fail: This program funds homeownership, not rentals.
NOHIP homes are for households at or below 80% AMI.

programs.name: Mandatory Inclusionary Zoning (MIZ)
programs.agency: City of New Orleans (Zoning Administration / City Planning Commission)
programs.summary: In MIZ sub-districts, residential projects of 10 or more units must set aside affordable units at 60% AMI for 99 years: 10% in the Core sub-district (CBD and Vieux Carré) and 5% in the Strong sub-districts. A fee in lieu is allowed under City Code Section 26-638. A November 2025 HR&A study recommended ending the mandate; check whether the Council has acted.
programs.eligibility: Applies to new multifamily rental projects with 10+ units inside a MIZ sub-district.

project_rules.fail: This program funds rental housing only.
Mandatory inclusionary zoning only applies to projects with 10 or more units.

programs.name: TIF district financing
programs.agency: City of New Orleans / district board
programs.summary: New Orleans' TIF districts capture future sales or property tax growth to pay for projects inside the district. They are typically set up around a specific development, so new projects would need to negotiate with the district.
programs.eligibility: Only for projects inside the district boundary.

programs.name: Historic District Landmarks Commission design review
programs.summary: Exterior work and new construction in a local historic district need HDLC approval. Budget time for design review; being in a historic district can also unlock the state historic credit and RTA.
programs.eligibility: Applies to sites inside a local historic district.

home.note: The City of New Orleans is a HOME participating jurisdiction and receives HOME funds directly from HUD.

cdbg.note: The City of New Orleans is a CDBG entitlement community; it awards CDBG through its own NOFAs.

cost_per_unit.note: Recent New Orleans LIHTC deals: Canal Crossing Senior (about $385k/unit) and Esplanade Delille (about $394k/unit) in LHC's 2026 programs report.

rent.note: HUD FY2026: 60% AMI 2-bedroom max rent is $1,197/month (60% limit $47,880 for 3 people), less about $100 for utilities.

opex.note: Estimate; no official local benchmark found. Insurance is high here: Gulf Coast affordable properties averaged $1,205/unit in 2023.

dscr.note: Louisiana Housing Corporation underwriting keeps debt coverage between 1.15 and 1.40.

lihtc_price.note: 2026 national LIHTC pricing: Novogradac Q1 2026 medians $0.80-$0.89; mid-2026 survey average 82.7 cents.
